subject: Activation verification and runbook playback for private deployment
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Activation verification and runbook playback for private deployment

Hi Elena / Acme Ops team,

We’re green to proceed with the scheduled activation window tomorrow 04/13 02:00-03:00 UTC. Attached is activation-runbook-v3.md — please confirm you received it and that your network team can commit to the timed steps. Key items we will validate during the playback:

- BGP session establishment and route propagation (announce /64s and confirm AS path)
- DNS switchover for api.acme.example (TTL and authoritative glue checks)
- L4 firewall ACLs (source CIDR, ports 443/2201 for admin) and any implicit deny rules
- MTU and jumbo frame consistency across the cross-connect (1500 vs 9000 mismatch causes fragmentation)
- NTP sync within 2s drift across primary boxes
- Syslog / audit forwarding to your collector (host: logs.acme-corp:514)
- Observability: token-level ingress metrics, p95 latency, error-rate spikes, KV cache hit-rate metric presence
- Rollback triggers: sustained p95 > 250ms for 5m, auth failure spike >2% or BGP flap >3 resets in 10m

Proposed lightweight playback order (we’ll run line-by-line):
1) Pre-checks (network reachability, DNS lookups, cert validity)
2) Stand up BGP session in maintenance mode (announce but do not change DNS)
3) Bring app endpoints into traffic gradually (10/30/60% cutover)
4) Full DNS switch and traffic cut
5) Post-activation validation (healthcheck endpoints, telemetry, logs)

If any pre-check fails we abort and go to roll-forward notes in the runbook. Can you confirm: who will be the on-prem firewall owner (name + pager), and can your team run a basic mtudump and share results before 02:00 UTC?

Attachments: activation-runbook-v3.md (runbook), netdiag-output.txt (example from staging)

Thanks — Connor
Connor O'Brien
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0137

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, IT Operations <ops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Activation verification and runbook playback for private deployment

Thanks Connor — we got the runbook. A couple quick clarifying Qs from Acme Ops before we lock the window:

1) NTP: who owns the authoritative NTP server on Redwood side? We need to ensure symmetric config vs our GPS-backed servers.
2) Syslog: can Redwood push logs over TLS (rsyslog RELP/forwarder) or do you expect plain TCP/UDP? We prefer TLS.
3) MTU: we will run mtudump but can you confirm the minimum MTU your agents accept? We’ve had issues with 9000->1500 mismatches in previous projects.
4) If we need to open an on-prem firewall temporary exception, do you have a vendor ticket template we can hand to our network partner?

Also: please include the post-activation checklist items you want filled in the final e-mail so our change board has a single artifact.

Elena Ruiz
Director, Infrastructure — Acme Corp
elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com

On Mon, Apr 12, 2027 at 09:12 AM Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai> wrote:
> We’re green to proceed with the scheduled activation window tomorrow 04/13 02:00-03:00 UTC...

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Activation verification and runbook playback for private deployment

Elena — good questions, answers inline below and I’ve added a short pre-check checklist you can paste to your change ticket.

1) NTP: Redwood agents will sync to the Redwood NTP cluster (ntp1.redwood.example / ntp2.redwood.example) by default; we can switch to symmetric mode to point at Acme GPS servers during the window. We’ll validate offset <2s before cut.
2) Syslog: we can push over TLS (we support syslog TLS/relp). I’ll include TLS instructions in the runbook appendix and cert fingerprint.
3) MTU: agents accept minimum MTU=1500. If you have 9000 on the cross-connect we’ll request the fabric to negotiate 1500 for the L2 path when needed; that’s in the pre-checks.
4) Firewall vendor ticket: attached runbook includes a one-paragraph vendor ticket body (search for "Firewall vendor ticket" section). Feel free to copy/paste.

Pre-check checklist (paste into your change board):
- Verify management plane reachability to 10.8.2.1:2201 from Acme ops NAT
- Confirm BGP neighbor IPs reachable (tcp 179 no-filter)
- DNS lookups for api.acme.example against new authoritative name-server
- TLS cert valid and chain present (openssl s_client -connect ...)
- MTU parity check: ping -s 1472 -M do <peer> (expect no fragmentation)
- NTP offset <2s across primary nodes

We’ll also run a short telemetry baseline 30m before the window and save it to the activation artifact (drive link included).

I’ll be on the call for the playback. Connor

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Activation verification and runbook playback for private deployment

Looping in a few observability and rollback guardrails from the ops playbook so they’re visible in the thread:

Observability bakeoff items (must be validated during step 5 - post-activation validation):
- Token ingestion rate and token-level cost metrics (ensure tags include customer_id:acme)
- KV cache hit-rate metric present and >= 65% for the first 10m under low load test (we’ll inject a 5qps synthetic workload)
- Tracing: sample traces from inference path show app->model runtime < 40ms per call for warm cache paths
- Log forwarding: confirm logs arrive at logs.acme-corp within 90s and contain request_id fields
- Alerts: configure temporary alert: p95 latency > 180ms -> Pager to (ops@acme-corp.com) and Redwood on-call (rotating)

Rollback triggers (explicit — if any occur we roll back immediately):
- p95 latency > 250ms sustained for 5 contiguous minutes
- Authentication failures spike to >2% of total requests in 5 minutes
- BGP session resets >3 in 10 minutes across any routed ASN

Contacts for playback (who we call if rollback):
- Elena Ruiz (Acme) — pager on ticket
- Connor O'Brien (Redwood) — +1 415-555-0137
- Marissa Cole (Redwood, PM) — marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Can the Acme team also run the dry-run of the script in your pre-prod cluster tonight? If pre-prod passes we’ll be comfortable with the full window.

Marissa
Director, Platform PM — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, IT Operations <ops@acme-corp.com>, Acme Network Consultant <net-consult@thirdparty.net>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Activation verification and runbook playback for private deployment — activation results

Team — activation complete. Quick post-activation verification summary (results copied into the change ticket):

Pre-checks and BGP
- BGP established: yes (peer up within 45s). Routes propagated to core (verified via show ip bgp).
- One small route-map typo on our side prevented community tagging initially; fixed at 02:12 UTC.

MTU and connectivity
- MTU mismatch detected on a transit switch (9000->1500); we forced 1500 on L2 fabric for the path at 02:05 UTC, fragmentation eliminated.

DNS / traffic cut
- DNS TTL lowered beforehand; final switch at 02:20 UTC. Traffic cut completed 02:20-02:27 in staged ramp (10/30/60/100). No 5xx spike during ramp.

Observability
- Token ingestion and tagging: pass (customer_id tag present).
- KV cache hit-rate: 69% during synthetic 5qps test.
- p95 latency post-cut: 62ms (baseline 58ms), no sustained spikes beyond thresholds.
- Logs forwarded to logs.acme-corp within 48s, request_id present.

Issues and actions
- ACL needed a temporary open to 10.9.4.2:2201 for vendor debugging; we tightened it immediately after verification.
- Netdiag attached (netdiag-output.txt).

Conclusion / next steps
- All major validation items pass. We’ll maintain heightened monitoring for 24 hours and run a short post-mortem next week to capture the route-map typo cause and tighten the ACL playbook.

Thanks for the clear runbook. Can Redwood prepare a short post-activation artifact we can attach to the change ticket (template list of checks + timestamps)?

Elena Ruiz
Director, Infrastructure — Acme Corp
